stories.title: Iran claims Hormuz closure, U.S. says ships still passing
stories.summary: Iran says it has closed the Strait of Hormuz again. The U.S. military says traffic is still flowing. NPR's Jane Arraf reports from Beirut.

stories.title: Israel's growing fight over Palestinian symbols
stories.summary: For some it's a symbol of identity. For others, a challenge to the state. NPR's Itay Stern reports on the debate over the Palestinian flag in Israel.

stories.title: The cruelty behind 'Minnesota nice'
stories.summary: George Floyd's murder put Minneapolis in the spotlight. Justin Ellis' new book, 'The Cruelty of Nice Folks: Why Minneapolis is the Story of America,' says the city embodies a contradiction - liberal ideals alongside deep racial disparities.

stories.title: For Pakistan's Ismaili muslims, a visit from their spiritual leader brings a homecoming
stories.summary: For many Ismaili Muslims, seeing the Aga Khan is a once-in-a-lifetime event. NPR's Betsy Joles reports from his visit to remote northern Pakistan.

stories.title: Butterflies may hold clues to longer lives
stories.summary: Why do some butterflies live for months while others survive only weeks? Tufts University researcher Jessica Foley explains what Heliconius butterflies can teach us about aging.

stories.title: U.S. defeats Australia in a key World Cup game
stories.summary: The United States defeated Australia in an important group match at the World Cup. The 2-0 victory means the U.S. will advance to the tournament's knockout round.
